blocks.text: The hidden cost of a bloated backlog

A messy backlog is not just a list of items. It is a source of constant cognitive load. Every time you open Jira, you process dozens of items that are no longer relevant. This searching and filtering consumes hours of your week.

When you let items sit, they grow stale. A user story written three months ago often requires a full refresh of context. This is what teams call failure demand. You spend your day fixing past mistakes instead of creating new value.

items: Input rates consistently exceed your team capacity.
The backlog is treated as a diary for every stakeholder idea.
Lack of a firm definition of ready for new items.
Fear of deleting items that might be useful later.

blocks.text: You do not need new software to fix this. You need better habits. Start by setting a hard limit on how many items can exist in the grooming column. If the limit is hit, you must move or delete an item before adding a new one.

Use your calendar to block two hours every Friday for a deep clean. During this time, look for items that have not been touched in 30 days. If they are not critical, move them to a separate archive project or delete them. Clarity is better than completeness.

faq.question: How can I speed up Jira tasks on Mac?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts in your browser. In Jira, press / to search and g then i to go to your issues. Use Lazur to dictate requirements directly into the description fields.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Jira?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac screen. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything visible, or use the fn key to dictate text into any Jira field.
